meta.title: Class Rides Along the Coast and Finds a Lost Bag

paragraphs: Class Rides Along the Coast and Finds a Lost Bag. By Lily, with a photo from Tom. Last week, Tom's class rode their bikes along the coast to a campsite. Tom is thirteen years old. He is in the older part of our school. Teacher Nick and Coach Matt rode with the children. A small truck carried the bags. The riding started at the school gate at seven o'clock in the morning. The group rode for four hours, with two short stops. The trip was on Saturday and Sunday. It was the first long ride of the year.

"The ride was not easy, because the sun was hot," Tom said. "We rode slowly, so everybody could keep up," he added. The sea was next to the road for most of the way. The road went up and down. The riders drank a lot of water. At the first stop, Coach Matt gave every child a banana and a bottle of water. Teacher Nick checked the bikes, and nearly all of them were fine. Nobody rode alone. One bike had a flat tire, and Coach Matt fixed it. The group arrived at the campsite at noon.

Then Hugo had a problem. His bag was not in the truck. It was not under the bikes. Hugo looked in the truck again, but the bag was not there. It was a bright orange bag with all his stuff: his lunch, his flashlight, and a warm shirt. The bag fell from his bike on the road. Nobody saw it. Hugo sat on the grass and did not say a word. Then Hugo said, "My stuff is lost!" Tom said, "Do not worry. We can look for it."

Coach Matt took two riders back along the road. One of them was Tom. Coach Matt rode fast, but Tom stayed next to him. After twenty minutes, they saw something orange next to a stone. It was the bag, and they found it easily because the color was so bright. The lunch was a little flat, but everything else was fine. The road was empty, so it was easy to see. Hugo thanked everybody immediately. Then he put the bag in his tent.

On Saturday night, the class ate rice and chicken near the tents. Then the class slept in tents near the beach. They rode home on Sunday. Teacher Nick says that every rider will check the bag before the next ride. Do you ride a bike to school or to a park? Tell us about your rides in a message!
